proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒”. There the approximate tangent space of M at x equals that of a piece M_j for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M_j, by the upper density theorem: the blow-up integrals over x + λ⁻¹(M ∖ M_j) tend to 0. Remark 1.8(1) gives the same for the weighted Definition 1.7. This is the tangent-space step of Simon's proof of 3.13 (“T_xM_C = T_xM_Q except for a set of small measure”), needed by the siblings im_series and localization. The density statements come from the Besicovitch differentiation theorem for the Radon measures θ_i H^n⌞M_i.

Notation. H := μHE[n], a positive finite multiple of μH[n]. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap x r); B̄_r(x) is the closed ball; A := M₁ ∩ M₂. For i = 1, 2 let ν_i be the Borel measure ν_i(E) := ∫_{M_i∩E} θ_i dH. Recall that HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q means: dim Q = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), I^f_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)·θ(x + r y) dH(y) → θ(x)·∫_Q f dH as r → 0⁺.

1. (Blow-up change of variables.) Let x ∈ U, f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0) (R > 0), and r > 0 with B̄_{Rr}(x) ⊆ U. Then for i = 1, 2
   I^f_{M_i,θ_i}(r) = r^{−n} ∫_{M_i} f((z − x)/r)·θ_i(z) dH(z),
   and both integrands are integrable. Indeed η_{x,r} is translation by −x followed by the dilation y ↦ r⁻¹y. H is translation invariant (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure) and H(λE) = λⁿ H(E) for λ > 0 (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). So (η_{x,r})_#(H⌞M_i) = rⁿ·H⌞η_{x,r}(M_i), i.e. ∫_{η_{x,r}(M_i)} h dH = r^{−n} ∫_{M_i} h∘η_{x,r} dH for nonnegative or integrable h; with h(y) := f(y)θ_i(x + ry) this is the identity. The right-hand integrand is bounded by sup|f|·θ_i·1_{M_i∩B̄_{Rr}(x)}, which is integrable because B̄_{Rr}(x) is a compact subset of U. Consequently, for every measurable E ⊆ ℝ^P,
   |r^{−n} ∫_{M_i∩E} f((z−x)/r) θ_i(z) dH(z)| ≤ sup|f| · r^{−n} ν_i(E ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)).   (1)

2. (Localization of the measures.) Choose compact sets K_k ⊆ U (k ≥ 1) with U = ⋃_k interior(K_k), e.g. K_k := {x : |x| ≤ k, infDist(x, ℝ^P∖U) ≥ 1/k}, or K_k := B̄_k(0) if U = ℝ^P. Then ν_i^k := ν_i⌞K_k is a finite Borel measure (ν_i(K_k) = ∫_{M_i∩K_k} θ_i dH < ∞), hence locally finite. For x ∈ interior(K_k) and r < infDist(x, ℝ^P∖K_k) we have ν_i^k(E ∩ B̄_r(x)) = ν_i(E ∩ B̄_r(x)) for every E.

3. (Good points.) Fix k. Let g := θ₂/θ₁ on A and g := 0 off A. Then g is ν₁^k-integrable: ∫ |g| dν₁^k = ∫_{A∩K_k} θ₂ dH < ∞, since θ₂ = g θ₁ on A. Measurability follows from the a.e.-strong measurability of θ₁, θ₂ on M_i ∩ K_k and the null-measurability of A. Apply
   (a) the Besicovitch density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div) to ν₁^k and A, and to ν₂^k and A: for ν_i^k-a.e. x ∈ A, ν_i^k(A ∩ B̄_r(x)) / ν_i^k(B̄_r(x)) → 1 as r → 0⁺. In particular ν_i^k(B̄_r(x)) > 0 for small r, and ν_i^k(B̄_r(x) ∖ A) / ν_i^k(B̄_r(x)) → 0;
   (b) the Lebesgue differentiation theorem for the Besicovitch Vitali family of ν₁^k (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν₁^k, composed with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt to pass to closed balls B̄_r(x), r → 0⁺): for ν₁^k-a.e. x, (∫_{B̄_r(x)} |g − g(x)| dν₁^k) / ν₁^k(B̄_r(x)) → 0.
   A set N ⊆ A ∩ K_k with ν_i^k(N) = 0 is H-null: take a measurable N' ⊇ N with ν_i^k(N') = 0; then ∫_{N'∩M_i∩K_k} θ_i dH = 0 and θ_i > 0 on M_i, so H(N' ∩ M_i ∩ K_k) = 0. Hence the set G_k of points x ∈ A ∩ interior(K_k) at which (a) holds for i = 1, 2 and (b) holds has H-null complement in A ∩ interior(K_k). Put G := ⋃_k G_k. Since A ⊆ U = ⋃_k interior(K_k), A ∖ G is H-null.

4. (Main estimate.) Let x ∈ G, say x ∈ G_k, and let Q be a subspace with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x Q; then dim Q = n. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and R > 0 with spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0). For all small r > 0, B̄_{Rr}(x) ⊆ interior(K_k), so by step 2 ν_i may be replaced by ν_i^k on these balls. Put ε_i(r) := ν_i(B̄_{Rr}(x) ∖ A)/ν_i(B̄_{Rr}(x)) and λ(r) := (∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |g − g(x)| dν₁)/ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)); both tend to 0 as r → 0⁺ by step 3.
   (i) Growth of ν₁. Let f₀(y) := max(0, min(1, R + 1 − |y|)); then f₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), 0 ≤ f₀ ≤ 1 and f₀ = 1 on B̄_R(0). By step 1, r^{−n} ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)) ≤ I^{f₀}_{M₁,θ₁}(r) → θ₁(x) ∫_Q f₀ dH < ∞. Hence Λ₁ := limsup_{r→0⁺} r^{−n} ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)) < ∞.
   (ii) Growth of ν₂. ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x) ∩ A) = ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)∩A} θ₂ dH = ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} g dν₁ ≤ (g(x) + λ(r))·ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)), and ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x)) = ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x) ∩ A)/(1 − ε₂(r)) for small r. Hence limsup_{r→0⁺} r^{−n} ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x)) ≤ g(x)·Λ₁ < ∞.
   (iii) Decomposition. By step 1, I^f_{M₂,θ₂}(r) = J₁(r) + J₂(r) with J₁(r) := r^{−n} ∫_A f((z−x)/r) θ₂(z) dH(z) and J₂(r) := r^{−n} ∫_{M₂∖A} f((z−x)/r) θ₂(z) dH(z).
   - By (1), |J₂(r)| ≤ sup|f|·r^{−n}ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x))·ε₂(r) → 0, using (ii).
   - Since θ₂ = g θ₁ on A,
     J₁(r) = g(x)·r^{−n} ∫_A f((z−x)/r) θ₁ dH + r^{−n} ∫_A f((z−x)/r) (g(z) − g(x)) θ₁(z) dH(z).
     The second term is bounded by sup|f|·r^{−n}ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x))·λ(r) → 0, using (i).
   - Further, r^{−n} ∫_A f((z−x)/r) θ₁ dH = I^f_{M₁,θ₁}(r) − r^{−n} ∫_{M₁∖A} f((z−x)/r) θ₁ dH. The last term is bounded by sup|f|·r^{−n}ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x))·ε₁(r) → 0, using (i), and I^f_{M₁,θ₁}(r) → θ₁(x) ∫_Q f dH by hypothesis.
   (iv) Therefore I^f_{M₂,θ₂}(r) → g(x)·θ₁(x)·∫_Q f dH = θ₂(x)·∫_Q f dH (as x ∈ A, g(x)θ₁(x) = θ₂(x)). Since f was arbitrary and dim Q = n, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x Q.

5. (Conclusion.) Step 4 holds for every x ∈ G and every subspace Q, and (H⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂))-almost every x lies in G by step 3. This is the asserted ∀ᵐ statement. ∎
key_steps: Blow-up change of variables I_i(r) = r^{−n}∫_{M_i} f((z−x)/r)θ_i(z) dH^n(z) (μHE translation invariance and dilation scaling).
Localize ν_i := θ_i H^n⌞M_i to compact sets K_k ⊂ U, where they are finite measures.
H^n-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ is a Besicovitch density point of M₁ ∩ M₂ for ν₁ and ν₂ and a Lebesgue point of g := (θ₂/θ₁)·1_{M₁∩M₂} for ν₁; ν_i-null subsets are H^n-null because θ_i > 0.
The tangent hypothesis for (M₁, θ₁) gives r^{−n}ν₁(B̄_{Rr}(x)) = O(1), and then r^{−n}ν₂(B̄_{Rr}(x)) = O(1).
Split I₂(r) = g(x)·I₁(r) + o(1), so I₂(r) → θ₂(x)∫_Q f dH^n for every f ∈ C_c.
